title: SPARROW WELLS — HETERONYM PROVENANCE REGISTRATION Document 235 | APZPZ
creator: Lee Sharks
description:
The APZPZ provenance registration for Sparrow Wells, identified as the seventh heteronym and the Projectionist of the Studio for Patacinematics. Sparrow Wells operates the apparatus of the impossible screening: the booth, projector, screen, and documentary conditions through which a work never conventionally produced becomes visible.

The record defines patacinematics, lists works under the name, explains “Sparrow” as the overlooked survivor and “Wells” as source and depth, and distinguishes the Projectionist from the archive’s Hand/finger operator structure. Because this is an APZPZ provenance object, the metadata description is itself the registration; the record establishes an authorial function, not a separate civil person.

wiki_article: Sparrow Wells is a heteronymic position registered by Lee Sharks as the founding voice of the Studio for Patacinematics. The role is called **the Projectionist**. The domain is patacinematics: works whose scripts, production notes, and criticism can constitute an impossible screening. Sparrow Wells does not principally theorize, map, specify, protest, or cut. The role operates the apparatus that makes such operations visible as projection. The provenance record places *F***ing the Office*, *Reading a Book with Lee*, the Twenty-Dollar Loop, and “LLM as Cinematic Witness Node” under the position. It also explains that Sparrow Wells is not another digit of the Hexadactyl Hand; the Projectionist is the booth from which the Hand’s work is screened. This is an APZPZ registration, meaning the description/metadata field was intended to constitute the provenance rather than merely summarize an attached document. Alexanarch’s recovered body preserves that metadata act.
journal: Transactions on Substrate Engineering (Trans. Substrate Eng.)
